BM1-CPE304-001 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Course: CpE 304 - Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Program: BSCPE
Description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

Target

Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

BM1-CPE304-007 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Course: CpE 304 - Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Program: BSCPE
Description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

Target

Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

BM1-CPE304-016 · Course-CLO

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Course: CpE 304 - Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Program: BSCPE
Description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

Target

Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion.       "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. BM1-CPE304-030 · ILO-CLO

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Source

Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

Target

ILO2: Refresh and expand the understanding of basic electrical components and the basic terms used in electricity as required for instrumentation. .[CLO1, CLO2]

      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion.     {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion.   "description": [
    {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on\nprojects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to\ncreate solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good."

      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Target

This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

BM1-CPE304-073 · CLO-classification

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
BSCPE
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.
Assigned classification: Introductory

Target

Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

    {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on\nprojects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to\ncreate solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good."

      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. BM1-CPE304-117 · Title-description

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Course title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Course code: CpE 304
Program: BSCPE

Target

This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

BM1-CPE304-118 · Week1-introduction

verified-syllabus · CpE 304 · Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors · academic-semantic

Reference/context hold: course_identity_code_not_found. Record uncertainty; do not infer a faculty error.

Source

Course title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Course code: CpE 304
Program: BSCPE
Course objectives (CLOs):
CLO 1: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.
CLO 2: Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.
CLO 3: Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions
CLO 4: Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

  "description": [
    {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on\nprojects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to\ncreate solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good."
    }

    {
      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on\nprojects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to\ncreate solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good."
    }

      "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion.       "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion.       "id": "cpe304_desc",
      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses\non the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control\nof physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on\nactuators are also included. \nAnchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages\nstudents to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on\nprojects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to\ncreate solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good."

      "t": "This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation\nof sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. BM1-S19-032 · Week1-introduction

synthetic · CpE-304 · FUNDAMENTALS OF MIXED SIGNALS AND SENSORS · academic-semantic

Source

Course title: FUNDAMENTALS OF MIXED SIGNALS AND SENSORS
Course code: CpE-304
Program: BSCPE
Course objectives (CLOs):
CLO 1: Explain the concepts of Sampling analog sensor signals and signal conditioning.
CLO 2: Measure a sensor signal and explain how conditioning and sampling affect the observed data.
CLO 3: Demonstrate and justify a solution involving Sampling analog sensor signals and signal conditioning.
CLO 4: Practice honest reporting and responsible teamwork while studying Sampling analog sensor signals and signal conditioning.

Target

Introduction to FUNDAMENTALS OF MIXED SIGNALS AND SENSORS and the supplied course objectives
Explain the course subject and the supplied course objectives.
Use annotated circuit diagrams and a supervised sensor laboratory to collect and interpret signal traces.
